Another little excursion into AI botland…

I’ve looked, almost a decade now, for thinkers who seriously critiqued the concept/device of authority as catastrophically self-defeating by its very nature and design.

I’ve looked for almost a decade for anyone who even knows of a thinker who seriously critiqued the concept/device of authority as catastrophically self-defeating by its very nature and design.

Results: nichts.

I needed a break from my project today, so, seeing as how they have upgraded ChatGPT, I thought I’d give the new and improved version a test drive.

Imagine that! Now the “intelligence” can actually remember information from chat to chat! Hopefully, this is the last time I’ll need to scold it for mansplaining, lol.

Here’s our chat on the question whether anyone has critiqued authority as intrinsically self-defeating to the extent of guaranteeing catastrophic failure by its very nature and design.

By that, I mean on the order of sprinkling arsenic on your oatmeal in order to sweeten it.

I asked two questions:

    1. Has anyone explained how authority is the substitution of command for competence?

It did give me some names on that one. So, that idea should not be controversial. The fact that it’s very controversial to most people is evidence of their membership in the Cult of Authority—but it says nothing about authority’s actual nature and design, nor anything about how authority actually works in the real world.

   2. Has anyone clearly explained in systems theory terms how "authority" is catastrophically self-defeating by its very design?

Isn’t it just mind-blowing that the key device for the operation of everything we’ve ever called a “civilization” or an “organization” has been predicated on an idea which NO ONE HAS EVER SERIOUSLY EXAMINED TO SEE IF IT’S FANTASTIC OR A FUBAR???

“Hey! I’ve got a great new flying machine based on a concept that no one has ever analyzed, let alone tested! But don’t worry! Everyone knows that it’s bulletproof! (Or, at least, the best we know how to do!)  COME ON! Let’s pack up the family and fly to Australia for holiday!”

Sure, why not? What could go wrong?

So, this is in honor of all the law-and-order cultists who, when I tried to open conversations about this topic, treated the idea as if it came from a mental ward patient. 😆

https://chatgpt.com/share/c8c47727-bf3c-4c60-b2fa-5a93638c1daf

comment.body:
For a long time I've had an idea that we have a kind of spiritual sanctuary within each one of us which is our holiest of holies. In our culture, we routinely violate and trespass into each other’s sanctuaries, and this kind of transgression_this sin—is superglued to our perverted concepts of power. 

I was thinking just now about being judged, and I realized that our typical response to being judged is to defend ourselves against the judgment, which means we're meeting the judge on the playfield of their definition and choosing, and we’re ascribing validity both to their judgment and to their qualifications to act as judge. 

Instead, we need to remove ourselves from that predicament, which is under their control, not remain stuck in it trying to defend against them and prove them wrong. 

What's more, when we remain in their bailiwick struggling to overcome their transgression, we almost invariably respond in kind by violating them in the same way that they are violating us in judging us. We do this by making the same kinds of unfounded and overreaching assertions about them and their judgment that are just as factually baseless and epistemologically unfounded and indefensible as is their judgment of us. 

Instead, the first thing we need to do is get them to state their qualifications for passing judgment on us. What are their facts, what is their familiarity with the events they're judging, and how much experience have they had in similar situations? 

If they don't have good answers to those questions, they are in no way qualified to judge us. 

If they have no answers at all, good or bad, for those questions, then they are only pretending to judge us. There’s no legitimate question about the validity and value of their judgment when it is, in fact, a lie. It's not real judgment. 

This is what most people are doing most of the time when they judge us. They’re not pronouncing an intelligent conclusion drawn from intelligent evaluation of anything relevant or real. 

They’re just fucking lying.

Undoubtedly, they’re applying rules or "truths" or laws—which they subscribe to in exactly the same way as do cultists to their dogmas—that to them (superficially) seem relevant and which they want to impose on us. 

That's not judgment, not in an evaluative sense, but rather naked, crass imposition of priorities and values that they're trying to force onto us or even into us. 

The attempt to do this and the act of doing it, among other things, is called "defilement" and "desecration". Such people have no business intruding at all, (if anyone ever does,) and to hell with what they have to say. 

Being such, their actions and what they say and all the arguments surrounding its correctness and rightness are absolutely irrelevant -- other than as proof of violation.

Here’s a question for you…

If you had to guess, which kind of people have been responsible for supporting and perpetrating every war, genocide, mass atrocity, and tyrannical regime ever known to humankind?

All the way down the line, none of this heinousness would ever have gotten off the ground without, and all of it was the responsibility of, a peculiar kind of people.

Which kind? I’ll let you ponder that a moment.

Criminals?

Traitors?

Terrorists?

…

No.

Patriots.

Lovers of country.

Lovers of “my people”.

None other.

So, now you can see—if you’re truly willing to look—what the origins and essence are of patriotism and so-called “love” of one’s preferred in-group.

And what characterizes those origins and this venomous nonsense they call “love”?

Murder.

And how do I know that? 

Well, the same way that we all know that.

What’s the first urge that these vile cultists feel whenever another “people” (as defined by their cult even if not by the “people” themselves) get in the way of or oppose or threaten “us good guys”—even if they have no intention of opposing or harming and are nothing resembling a credible threat?

Sure, if the “patriots” aren’t too freaked out and not sufficiently full of bile, spite, and hatred, they might try “diplomacy” first. 

But we all know, just as they do, what their real MO is: they stand ready, even eager, to kill.

Of course! Because, otherwise, what else could they do against such despicable enemies?

I call that an argument from ignorance and stupidity.

“We know of nothing more reliable, effective, and final than killing!”

Well, that puts them in very specialized company, and it’s not of the one they think they’re “serving”.

These are some sad and sorry, weak little bitches.

This is why patriotism is evil.

This is why “love” of country and “my people” is evil.

So, I wonder: what do you think of the 4th of July now, with its grandiose mimicry of bombs bursting in air?

“Oooo… all the pretty lights!” 

??

comment.body:
I wanted to quantify something I realized decades ago, so I had a couple of AI chats about it this morning: the incredibly small, infinitesimal fraction of what’s really gone on that supports human knowledge.

You can see my chat with Gemini here (you have to scroll way up, the link takes you to the end of the chat):  https://gemini.google.com/app/2e65be7663b34d45

and the follow-up with ChatGPT here:  https://chat.openai.com/share/ea0eb17f-0e01-46c7-a628-6b5ee4f46db8

We arrived at a number: our “knowledge” is based on observations of only around 50 sextillionths of the universe. 

But that’s not all. We have to factor in the historical side, too. And then we have to factor in the faction of what people call “knowledge” that even takes into account that 50 sextillionths-worth of observations, “knowledge” having been mostly a matter of dogma, intuitions, hunches, guesses, tradition, myth which, in turn, is mostly based on a HUGE old pile of steaming bullshit that someones, somewheres, at some times just made the fuck up.

So, we arrived at 4.2 × 10 to the -27. No idea, right? Me neither. I asked ChatGPT to put that in human language.

A “trillionth of a trillionth of a trillionth”.

So, HOW THE FUCK do people get away with saying “I know” when you consider that we have a near-nonexistent basis in observed facts for anything we call “knowledge”?

This is why people “believe”.

When there’s no fucking way an person could credibly pretend there’s any real basis for “knowing”, but they want to proceed as if there were anyway, they say, “I believe that…”

Can you get an inkling of how dishonest, deceptive, and devious this stuff is that we call “knowledge”, and even worse, “belief”?

Everything we think we know is almost entirely bullshit, when you look at it like that.

We’ve got shitloads of hubris that most people consider “normal” for a “well-adjusted” person.

It stinks. And it makes people caked with the stuff glaring. See it, feel it, and smell it coming.

Most people are currently hanging from skyhooks in that lapse.

Instead of oozing smarm and hubris, they get upset; because now they know there probably are facts out there, maybe lots of them, but they don’t have a stinking clue what they are or how to find them.

Tough spot.
